posts.meta_description:
7,021 likes, 60 comments - nikhilkamathcio on October 25, 2026: "Is AI the biggest revolution of our lifetime, or just the most expensive bubble we’ve ever created?

Sat down with Akshay Kothari, co-founder of Notion ($11B), Vijay Krishnan, co-founder of Turing ($2.2B), and Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini, the former Google researchers who helped pioneer AI-designed chips and went on to build Ricursive Intelligence ($4B).

We went from hardware to training models to applications. Essentially, the entire AI food chain.

Is this all hype? Are our jobs going away? And more importantly, can India actually make money from any of this?

Figured I’d ask the people building it, rather than the people selling it.

Early to the revolution or late to the bubble?

Episode out now..".

16K likes, 128 comments - nikhilkamathcio on October 13, 2026: "UPI feels simple because most of what makes it work is invisible.

I followed one payment all the way through with Sameer Nigam (PhonePe), Harshil Mathur (Razorpay) and Sohini Rajola (NPCI): who moves the money, who pays the cost, and where fraud fits in. Then we argued about AI agents that could shop and pay for us.

What would you let an AI agent buy without asking you first?

Coming soon.".

13K likes, 113 comments - nikhilkamathcio on October 5, 2026: "Everyone in China says ‘ecosystem, ecosystem, ecosystem.’ Foundery is a small attempt at trying to build that for consumer brands in India. It’s not about how many of the 20 brands per batch succeed or what valuations they achieve, but about the fact that, in 10 years, we would have built the rails and the ‘ecosystem’ by attempting to create 200 Indian brands with the potential to sell globally..

@jointhefoundery".

posts.meta_description:
15K likes, 218 comments - nikhilkamathcio on September 28, 2026: "Korea exported culture. 
Then the world bought Korean…

India has Bollywood, music, food, fashion, yoga and Ayurveda, a cultural moat very few countries can replicate..
Maybe we need to stop thinking only about exporting products and start deliberately exporting India. 
Consumer brands could follow.".

posts.meta_description:
7,558 likes, 198 comments - nikhilkamathcio on September 20, 2026: "The test of a first-rate intelligence is the ability to hold two opposed ideas in the mind at the same time, and still retain the ability to function.” — F. Scott Fitzgerald

The internet increasingly rewards the angrier, louder side, the more certain-sounding side, often the stupider side.

Maybe intelligence is being able to understand why the other side believes what it believes.

Introducing WTF: Discourse.

Two opposing ideas. Two people who actually believe them. No winner. Just the strongest version of both arguments.

You decide what you believe.".

posts.meta_description:
14K likes, 156 comments - nikhilkamathcio on September 9, 2026: "India gets about 10 million foreign tourists a year.

Dubai gets 18 million.

Dubai is basically one long road. We are 1.4 billion people with the Himalayas, Goa, Rajasthan, Kerala, the Andamans, 5,000 years of history and arguably the best food in the world :)

Something doesn’t add up.

Two men who built India’s biggest travel and hotel businesses agree on one thing: the country is easy to leave, hard to visit.

India has transformed dramatically over the last decade, better roads, airports, digital infrastructure and connectivity. Maybe tourism is the next big opportunity.

In this episode, the CEOs of MakeMyTrip and IHCL (Taj Hotels) tell us 5 things that could get a lot more of the world to come visit India, and where the opportunities for entrepreneurs might lie along the way.

Episode out now..".

33K likes, 2,182 comments - nikhilkamathcio on September 4, 2026: "WTF Offline.

1 stadium. 10 hours. 150 people

No cameras, no press, no phones.

No audience either. Just friends and people I have had on the podcast over the years.

A safe space for conversations to happen differently when there’s no camera to perform for.

PS: We capped it at 150 people, partly to keep it intimate and partly because 151 onwards it starts to sound like the beginning of a cult :)".
